liabilities.label: Bank deposits, repos and bonds issued

balance.note: A bank's balance sheet is mostly other people's money: customer deposits fund the loans. Shareholders' funds are about 10% of assets, which is why capital ratios matter.

safety.label: CET1 capital ratio
safety.plain: The bank's own capital as a cushion against losses, as a share of its risk-weighted loans. Bank Negara's minimum is 4.5% plus buffers. As printed in the report's capital note; some banks print it before deducting the proposed dividend.

safety.label: Total capital ratio
safety.plain: All qualifying capital as a share of risk-weighted loans; the regulatory minimum is 8% plus buffers.

safety.label: Gross impaired loans
safety.plain: Loans in trouble as a share of all loans. Lower is better.

safety.label: Loan loss allowance coverage
safety.plain: Money already set aside for losses, compared with the troubled loans. Above 100% means fully covered.

safety.label: Loan to deposit ratio
safety.plain: The bank lends out about RM100 of every RM100 deposited.

safety.label: CASA ratio
safety.plain: Share of deposits in current and savings accounts, which pay little interest and keep funding cheap.

safety.label: Liquidity coverage ratio
safety.plain: Cash and easy-to-sell assets against 30 days of stressed outflows; the minimum is 100%.

metrics.label: Market value
metrics.plain: What the whole company costs at today's share price: RM87.0 billion.

metrics.label: P/E (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: You pay about RM12 for every RM1 of yearly profit. A high number means investors expect growth.

metrics.label: EPS (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: Profit earned for each share you own over the last year.

metrics.label: Dividend yield (dividends paid in the last 12 months)
metrics.plain: For every RM100 of shares, about RM5.0 a year comes back as cash dividends.

metrics.label: Payout ratio
metrics.plain: Of every RM100 profit, about RM60 is paid out; the rest is kept to grow.

metrics.label: Price to book
metrics.plain: The share price is 1.4 times the accounting value of what shareholders own.

metrics.label: Return on equity (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: For every RM100 shareholders have in the company, it earned about RM12 profit last year.

metrics.label: Net margin 9M2026
metrics.plain: What is left as profit for shareholders from every RM100 of revenue: RM47.52.

metrics.label: Revenue growth 9M2026
metrics.plain: Revenue compared with the same period a year earlier.

metrics.label: Profit growth 9M2026
metrics.plain: Profit to shareholders compared with the same period a year earlier.

metrics.label: Cost to income (9M2026)
metrics.plain: Of every RM100 of income, about RM35 is spent on staff, branches and IT. Lower is more efficient.

metrics.label: Credit cost (9M2026, annualised)
metrics.plain: Provisions for bad loans equal to 0.09% of loans a year. Lower is better.

drivers.factor: Loan growth from SMEs, cars and homes
drivers.evidence: Gross loans grew at an annualised 6.2% to RM466.5bn in 9M2026, led by domestic SME, hire purchase and residential financing (Q B1)
drivers.why: Its core retail lending keeps expanding.

drivers.evidence: Net income rose 2.6% in 9M2026 while costs rose 2.8% (database)
drivers.why: Revenue growth only just covers rising costs.

drivers.evidence: Loan provisions of RM294m in 9M2026 against RM84m a year earlier (database)
drivers.why: Profit was flat (+0.02%) despite higher income.

drivers.evidence: Gross impaired loans 0.55% at 30 September 2026 (Q B1)
drivers.why: Fewer losses and a reputation for prudence.

drivers.evidence: Public Mutual earned RM246.9m profit before tax in 3Q2026 alone (Q p.46)
drivers.why: Fee income that does not depend on interest rates.

drivers.evidence: Plan to take full ownership of its Hong Kong-listed unit PFHL, expected by 16 December 2026; management expects a positive effect on earnings per share (Q B3)
drivers.why: More of the overseas profit would belong to Public Bank shareholders.
Fewer cheap current and savings deposits than peers means higher funding cost.

outlook.text: Malaysian economy underpinned by domestic demand, investment projects and electronics exports (Q B3).
Banking sector resilient with ample liquidity; the group will keep prudence in credit risk (Q B3).
Downside risks from Middle East tensions, commodity price swings and trade fragmentation (Q B3).

outlookOverall.text: Management expects to keep its leading position in domestic retail banking while staying prudent in a more challenging environment (Q B3).
